Recognizing a dance through multiple characteristics

The most reliable way to distinguish Indian classical dances is to consider their region of origin together with their historical traditions, repertoire, musical accompaniment and visual characteristics. Many individual features are shared across different forms.

For example, both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi use Carnatic music and may have visually similar costumes. Kathak, Manipuri and Sattriya all draw substantially upon Krishna-related devotional traditions. These shared characteristics cannot identify a single dance without additional information.

Classical dance, traditional dance and UNESCO recognition

National classification of classical dance and international recognition of intangible cultural heritage are separate matters. UNESCO's inscription of a cultural practice does not automatically classify it as one of India's 8 principal classical dance forms.

The conventional 8-form classification is supported by the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training. However, cultural promotion and scholarship schemes may use broader administrative categories that include additional traditional dance forms such as Chhau. Therefore, the exact institution or classification named in a statement is important.

Chhau

Chhau is a traditional dance form of eastern India that combines narrative, martial elements and regional performance traditions. It has 3 major regional styles.

StyleStateTraditional use of masks
Purulia ChhauWest BengalUses masks
Seraikella ChhauJharkhandUses masks
Mayurbhanj ChhauOdishaDoes not use masks

UNESCO inscribed Chhau dance on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010. It is not included in the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training's conventional principal list of 8 classical forms, although it is included in broader cultural promotion and scholarship classifications.

Garba and Gujarat

Garba is a traditional participatory dance of Gujarat, particularly associated with Navratri and devotion to the feminine divine. UNESCO inscribed Garba of Gujarat on the Representative List in 2023.

Garba's international recognition does not make it one of the 8 principal classical dances of India.

Selected UNESCO inscriptions relevant to dance

Cultural elementInscription yearRegional association
Chhau dance2010West Bengal, Jharkhand and Odisha
Sankirtana, ritual singing, drumming and dancing of Manipur2013Manipur
Garba of Gujarat2023Gujarat

These are the original inscription years. All 3 elements remained listed on the UNESCO Representative List as consulted on 25 November 2026.

Prelims focus

  • Bhama Kalapam belongs to Kuchipudi; Gita Govinda is prominent in Odissi.
  • Chenda and Maddalam identify Kathakali; Pung identifies Manipuri; Khol identifies Sattriya.
  • Kerala is the origin of both Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.
  • Mayurbhanj Chhau is traditionally performed without masks.
  • UNESCO inscriptions: Chhau in 2010, Manipur Sankirtana in 2013 and Garba of Gujarat in 2023.
  • Trap: Sattriya's classical recognition in 2000 is not a UNESCO inscription.

The 8 principal classical dances at a glance

The regional grouping of classical dance forms reflects the diversity of Indian cultural traditions. Tamil Nadu is associated with Bharatanatyam; Andhra Pradesh with Kuchipudi; Kerala with Kathakali and Mohiniyattam; northern India with Kathak; Odisha with Odissi; Manipur with Manipuri; and Assam with Sattriya. Their continued practice across India makes classical dance a shared national heritage rather than an art confined to its original region.

[References: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training, performing arts overview and Scheme for Scholarships to Young Artistes; NCERT, Class 11, Living Craft Traditions of India, Theatre Crafts, pp. 113–115; CBSE, Class 12, Knowledge Traditions and Practices of India, Dance: A Survey, classical dance sections; UNESCO, Chhau Dance, 2010; UNESCO, Sankirtana, Ritual Singing, Drumming and Dancing of Manipur, 2013; UNESCO, Garba of Gujarat, 2023; UNESCO, India country inventory of inscribed intangible cultural heritage elements. Online sources consulted 25 November 2026.]
